Author: Bennett Matuszewski <164584687+bennettmatuszewski@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Wed Sep 30 18:02:39 2026 -0400

    [AI] Add CSV export for a budget month
    
    Add an Export button to the budget page titlebar (envelope budgets only)
    that downloads the selected month as <budget-name>-<YYYY-MM>.csv. When
    several months are shown, the menu lists one entry per visible month.
    
    The CSV lists every visible category group and category in page order
    with Budgeted, Spent and Balance columns, a subtotal row per group, a
    grand Total row and a To Budget / Overbudgeted summary. Values are read
    from the same spreadsheet cells the page displays, so carryover
    balances and totals match exactly. Hidden items follow the page's
    show-hidden toggle.
    
    Extract the csv-stringify call and formula-injection guard into a
    shared stringifyCsv helper, now also used by the Budget Analysis
    export, and share the visible-months calculation via getVisibleMonths.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    10	type BudgetMonthCells = Map<string, unknown>;
    11	
    12	type BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions = {
    13	  month: string;
    14	  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
    15	  cells: BudgetMonthCells;

    17	  decimalPlaces: number;

    20	type CsvRow = [string, string, number | '', number | '', number | ''];
    21	
    22	// Builds a CSV of one envelope budget month, mirroring the rows and values
    23	// shown on the budget page. Subtotals and totals come from the spreadsheet's
    24	// own group/total cells so they always match what the page displays.
    25	export function buildBudgetMonthCsv({
    26	  month,
    27	  categoryGroups,
    28	  cells,
    29	  showHiddenCategories,
    30	  decimalPlaces,
    31	}: BuildBudgetMonthCsvOptions): string {
    32	  function amount(value: number | null): number | '' {
    33	    return value == null ? '' : integerToAmount(value, decimalPlaces);
    34	  }
    35	
    36	  const rawRows = collectBudgetMonthRows({
    37	    month,
    38	    categoryGroups,
    39	    cells,
    40	    showHiddenCategories,
    41	  });
    42	
    43	  const rows: CsvRow[] = rawRows.map(row => [
    44	    row.groupName,
    45	    row.categoryName,
    46	    amount(row.budgeted),
    47	    amount(row.spent),
    48	    amount(row.balance),
    49	  ]);
    50	
    51	  return stringifyCsv(rows, [
    52	    t('Category Group'),
    53	    t('Category'),
    54	    t('Budgeted'),
    55	    t('Spent'),
    56	    t('Balance'),
    57	  ]);
    58	}
    59	
    60	export function getBudgetMonthExportFilename(
    61	  budgetName: string | undefined,
    62	  month: string,
    63	  extension: 'csv' | 'pdf',
    64	): string {
    65	  const safeName = (budgetName ?? '').replace(/[\\/:*?"<>|]/g, '').trim();
    66	  return `${safeName || 'budget'}-${month}.${extension}`;
    67	}
    68	
    69	export async function fetchBudgetMonthCells(
    70	  month: string,
    71	): Promise<BudgetMonthCells> {
    72	  const values = await send('envelope-budget-month', { month });
    73	  return new Map(values.map(({ name, value }) => [name, value]));

     1	// Use the browser ESM build: the default `csv-stringify/sync` entry pulls in
     2	// the Node build (which imports `stream`), breaking lazy-loaded chunks in the
     3	// browser bundle. The browser ESM build is self-contained.
     4	import { stringify as csvStringify } from 'csv-stringify/browser/esm/sync';
     5	
     6	// Values starting with these characters are interpreted as formulas by
     7	// spreadsheet apps, so they get a leading `'` to keep them as plain text.
     8	const FORMULA_TRIGGERS = /^[=+\-@\t\r]/;
     9	
    10	export function stringifyCsv(rows: unknown[][], columns: string[]): string {
    11	  return csvStringify(rows, {
    12	    header: true,
    13	    columns,
    14	    cast: {
    15	      string: (value: string) =>
    16	        FORMULA_TRIGGERS.test(value) ? "'" + value : value,
    17	    },
    18	  });
    19	}

     8	export type RawBudgetMonthRowKind =
     9	  | 'group'
    10	  | 'category'
    11	  | 'income'
    12	  | 'incomeCategory'
    13	  | 'total'
    14	  | 'toBudget';
    15	
    16	export type RawBudgetMonthRow = {
    17	  kind: RawBudgetMonthRowKind;
    18	  groupName: string;
    19	  // '' for group/total/toBudget rows.
    20	  categoryName: string;
    21	  // Raw integer cents read from the sheet cell, not yet scaled by the
    22	  // currency's decimal places. `null` means the page shows a blank cell.
    23	  budgeted: number | null;
    24	  spent: number | null;
    25	  balance: number | null;
    26	};
    27	
    28	type CollectBudgetMonthRowsOptions = {
    29	  month: string;
    30	  categoryGroups: CategoryGroupEntity[];
    31	  cells: Map<string, unknown>;
    32	  showHiddenCategories: boolean;
    33	};
    34	
    35	// Walks one envelope budget month's category groups/categories in page
    36	// order and reads their Budgeted/Spent/Balance values from the same
    37	// spreadsheet cells the page displays, so every consumer (CSV, PDF, ...)
    38	// shows identical numbers and can never drift apart.
    39	export function collectBudgetMonthRows({
    40	  month,
    41	  categoryGroups,
    42	  cells,
    43	  showHiddenCategories,
    44	}: CollectBudgetMonthRowsOptions): RawBudgetMonthRow[] {
    45	  const sheetName = monthUtils.sheetForMonth(month);
    46	
    47	  function cellValue(name: string) {
    48	    const value = cells.get(`${sheetName}!${name}`);
    49	    return typeof value === 'number' ? value : 0;
    50	  }
    51	
    52	  function isVisible(item: { hidden?: boolean }) {
    53	    return showHiddenCategories || !item.hidden;
    54	  }
    55	
    56	  const [expenseGroups, incomeGroup] = separateGroups(categoryGroups);
    57	  const rows: RawBudgetMonthRow[] = [];
    58	
    59	  for (const group of expenseGroups.filter(isVisible)) {
    60	    rows.push({
    61	      kind: 'group',
    62	      groupName: group.name,
    63	      categoryName: '',
    64	      budgeted: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupBudgeted(group.id)),
    65	      spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupSumAmount(group.id)),
    66	      balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupBalance(group.id)),
    67	    });
    68	
    69	    for (const category of (group.categories ?? []).filter(isVisible)) {
    70	      rows.push({
    71	        kind: 'category',
    72	        groupName: group.name,
    73	        categoryName: category.name,
    74	        budgeted: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catBudgeted(category.id)),
    75	        spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catSumAmount(category.id)),
    76	        balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catBalance(category.id)),
    77	      });
    78	    }
    79	  }
    80	
    81	  // The income group is always shown on the page, even when marked hidden.
    82	  if (incomeGroup) {
    83	    rows.push({
    84	      kind: 'income',
    85	      groupName: incomeGroup.name,
    86	      categoryName: '',
    87	      budgeted: null,
    88	      spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.groupIncomeReceived),
    89	      balance: null,
    90	    });
    91	
    92	    for (const category of (incomeGroup.categories ?? []).filter(isVisible)) {
    93	      rows.push({
    94	        kind: 'incomeCategory',
    95	        groupName: incomeGroup.name,
    96	        categoryName: category.name,
    97	        budgeted: null,
    98	        spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.catSumAmount(category.id)),
    99	        balance: null,
   100	      });
   101	    }
   102	  }
   103	
   104	  // `total-budgeted` is stored negated; the page flips it back for display.
   105	  rows.push({
   106	    kind: 'total',
   107	    groupName: t('Total'),
   108	    categoryName: '',
   109	    budgeted: -cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalBudgeted),
   110	    spent: cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalSpent),
   111	    balance: cellValue(envelopeBudget.totalBalance),

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-22 16:12:50Z)**_

The month CSV export came in with commit `43a6d9f39` (PR #71, issue #56). It doesn't calculate any numbers itself. It reads the values the budget page already displays, puts them in page order, and writes them out as a CSV. Two later commits for the PDF export (issues #60 and #61) moved the row-building into a shared file, so the CSV and the PDF now run through the same code.

## The pipeline

```
Titlebar → BudgetExportMenu → get-budget-bounds → menu of visible months
   → user picks "csv:2026-09"
   → fetchBudgetMonthCells   (backend: envelope-budget-month)
   → collectBudgetMonthRows  (walks the categories in page order)
   → buildBudgetMonthCsv     (turns cents into amounts, writes the CSV text)
   → window.Actual.saveFile  (browser download or Electron save dialog)
```

### 1. Where the button appears
[Titlebar.tsx:264](packages/desktop-client/src/components/Titlebar.tsx#L264) renders `<BudgetExportMenu />` only when `budgetType === 'envelope'`. Tracking budgets don't get it, because they use different spreadsheet cell names (`trackingParametrizedField` instead of `envelopeParametrizedField` in [bindings.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/spreadsheet/bindings.ts)).

### 2. Which months the menu offers
[BudgetExportMenu.tsx:97-102](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BudgetExportMenu.tsx#L97-L102) works out the visible months the same way the budget page does:
- The start month is the `budget.startMonth` local pref, or the current month if that isn't set.
- The month count is `min(displayMax, maxMonths)`, where `displayMax` is how many columns fit on screen.
- The range is limited to the budget's real bounds. The menu fetches those with `send('get-budget-bounds')` when you click Export, not when the page renders, so they're always current.

The range calculation is `getVisibleMonths`. You moved it out of `MonthsProvider` into [MonthsContext.tsx:23](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/MonthsContext.tsx#L23) so the page and the export share it and can't disagree.

`buildExportMenuItems` builds the menu. With one visible month you get a plain "Export as CSV" item. With several, you get a "CSV" section with one item per month. Each item's name encodes the action (`csv:2026-09`), and an `actions` Map looks the name up when you pick it.

### 3. Getting the numbers
`fetchBudgetMonthCells` ([budgetMonthCsv.ts:69](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthCsv.ts#L69)) calls the existing backend handler `envelope-budget-month` in [loot-core budget/app.ts:212](packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/app.ts#L212). That handler reads the sheet cells for the month (`budget-<id>`, `sum-amount-<id>`, `leftover-<id>`, the group totals, `to-budget` and so on) straight from the spreadsheet engine. The result becomes a `Map` keyed by full cell names like `budget202609!leftover-<catId>`.

Because these are the same cells the page displays, carryover, rollover, and overspending come through exactly as they appear on screen. Nothing is recomputed from transactions.

### 4. Building the rows
`collectBudgetMonthRows` ([budgetMonthRows.ts:39](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthRows.ts#L39)) walks the categories from `useCategories()`:
- **Expense groups:** a subtotal row per group (`group-budget`, `group-sum-amount`, `group-leftover`), followed by its categories.
- **Hidden items:** groups and categories marked hidden are skipped unless the page's `budget.showHiddenCategories` toggle is on.
- **Income group:** always included, even if it's marked hidden, because the page always shows it. Its rows have only a "Spent" (received) value. Budgeted and Balance are `null`, which becomes an empty cell.
- **Total row:** `total-budgeted` is stored as a negative number in the sheet, so it's negated back (line 109), the same way the page flips it for display.
- **Last row:** labelled "To Budget", or "Overbudgeted" when the value is negative.

Missing or non-numeric cells default to `0`.

### 5. Writing the CSV
`buildBudgetMonthCsv` ([budgetMonthCsv.ts:25](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthCsv.ts#L25)) converts each value from integer cents to an amount with `integerToAmount(value, decimalPlaces)`. It uses the currency's decimal places, so currencies with 0 or 3 decimal places come out right. It then passes the rows to `stringifyCsv` with translated column headers: Category Group, Category, Budgeted, Spent, Balance.

`stringifyCsv` ([util/csv.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/util/csv.ts)) is a helper you extracted, and the Budget Analysis report's export now uses it too. It does two things:
- It imports `csv-stringify/browser/esm/sync` instead of the default entry, because the default pulls in Node's `stream` and breaks lazy-loaded browser chunks.
- It guards against formula injection: any text starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading `'`. Without that, a category named `=HYPERLINK(...)` would run as a formula in Excel. Amounts stay numbers, so negative values aren't affected.

### 6. Saving the file
`getBudgetMonthExportFilename` removes characters that aren't allowed in filenames (`\/:*?"<>|`) from the budget name. If nothing is left, it uses `budget`, giving names like `My Budget-2026-09.csv`. `window.Actual.saveFile` then works differently by platform:
- **Browser** ([browser-preload.js:222](packages/desktop-client/src/browser-preload.js#L222)): creates a `Blob`, attaches it to a hidden `<a download>`, and clicks it.
- **Electron** ([preload.ts:54](packages/desktop-electron/preload.ts#L54)): sends `save-file-dialog` over IPC, which opens the native save dialog.

If anything throws along the way, `onMenuSelect` shows a generic "Failed to export the budget month." notification.

## Testing
[budgetMonthCsv.test.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/export/budgetMonthCsv.test.ts) builds a fake cell `Map` and checks the CSV output directly: row order, how hidden items are handled, the negated total, To Budget vs. Overbudgeted, and the formula guard. Because the builder doesn't depend on React, the tests don't need to render a component or mock the backend.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-22 16:31:31Z)**_

Yes, just one: **`csv-stringify`** (version 6.8.1, from the `csv` project on npm). It's what turns the rows into CSV text.

It comes in through [util/csv.ts:4](packages/desktop-client/src/util/csv.ts#L4):

```ts
import { stringify as csvStringify } from 'csv-stringify/browser/esm/sync';
```

- **Which build:** this is the synchronous browser ESM build, not the default `csv-stringify/sync` entry. The default one loads Node's `stream` module, which breaks lazy-loaded chunks in the browser bundle.
- **What the library does:** it adds the header row, escapes fields that contain commas, quotes or newlines, and joins the rows together.
- **What your code adds:** the formula-injection guard, which is a `cast.string` hook that puts `'` in front of risky text. The library doesn't do that on its own.

Your commit didn't add a new dependency. `csv-stringify` was already listed in [desktop-client/package.json:179](packages/desktop-client/package.json#L179) because the Budget Analysis report's export used it. Your change moved that call into the shared `stringifyCsv` helper so both exports use it.

The month export doesn't parse any CSV. The repo also has `csv-parse` in `loot-core`, but that's only for importing transactions.
